## Summary

I wrote `src/test/java/org/apache/commons/lang3/math/FractionAgentTest.java`, a self-contained JUnit 5 test class with 92 test methods covering all `Fraction` factory methods, arithmetic operations (`add`, `subtract`, `multiplyBy`, `divideBy`, `pow`, `invert`, `negate`, `abs`, `reduce`), comparisons, numeric conversions, `equals`/`hashCode`, and string formatting — including boundary cases (`Integer.MIN_VALUE`/`MAX_VALUE`, zero/negative denominators, overflow, `NaN`, null arguments, malformed strings).

All 92 tests pass. I also hand-verified several tricky areas against the implementation via a throwaway scratch probe (deleted afterward, not part of the deliverable): the Knuth add/subtract algorithm's BigInteger fallback path, `multiplyBy` cross-reduction, `pow` with negative/`MIN_VALUE` exponents, `reduce()`/`toProperString()` with `Integer.MIN_VALUE` numerators, and the binary-GCD's handling of `Math.abs(Integer.MIN_VALUE)` staying negative. Everything matched documented/expected behavior — I found no bugs in `Fraction` to leave a failing test for.
